summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: there are no confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks, but Iran is still attacking ships around the Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and talks on a new draft deal are under way. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: No US strikes on Iran since Sept 1. Trump said on Oct 8 there would be none before the Nov 3 midterms; reports say renewed strikes are being prepared for after that.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent near US$115 and WTI near US$101 on Oct 28, up more than 12% this month; the year high is near US$126.

updates.text: Qatari mediators gave Iran a new draft deal to end the war on Sunday (Oct 25). Iran is considering it and is expected to respond by the end of the week.
The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Taif. The Houthis also claimed a drone strike on Abha airport, not confirmed by Saudi Arabia.
Iran's navy said an oil tanker hit mines and caught fire, and that Hormuz is "unsafe and closed to rogue ships" passing without its coordination.

Fresh fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces near Bab el-Mandeb; the Saudi-led coalition said it downed two Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh. Egypt's parliament has authorized sending troops to Saudi Arabia.
UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported a tanker disabled by a projectile while outbound through Hormuz on Oct 23; the crew is safe. About 492 ships were waiting outside the strait on Oct 25.
Trump: "I have a decision to make: Do I finish it off, which would be very easy to do, or do I make a deal?" He also claimed the US now controls the strait.

October has seen the most attacks on ships since the war began: at least 12 in the week to Oct 16, per UKMTO. CENTCOM says the strait is controlled by the US and its partners; Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it is unsafe for ships that don't coordinate with Iran.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
